# Research Leads

Use this page to preserve source trails worth revisiting: publications, people, organizations, search terms, reports, and source types that repeatedly improve the wiki.

## Lead table

| Domain | Lead | Why it matters | Follow-up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ai-software | Official model, API, SDK, and product docs | Product and tooling details age quickly and should be checked at the source. | Verify before updating public-facing AI claims. |
| canada-policy | Canadian government, defence, infrastructure, and economic-policy primary sources | Policy claims need primary-source support before external use. | Prefer official docs and reports for [Canadian Prosperity Agenda](/wiki/canadian-prosperity-agenda). |
| health | Primary health, sleep, longevity, and occupational-health sources | Health claims can become misleading without current evidence. | Treat practitioner claims as leads, not facts. |
| venture | Customer language, procurement pages, job posts, forums, and buyer interviews | Venture pages need demand evidence, not only creator claims. | Connect leads to [Venture Opportunity Discovery](/wiki/venture-opportunity-discovery). |
| communication | Strong speeches, campaigns, and writing craft sources | Communication pages benefit from concrete examples and repeatable models. | Route durable frameworks to [Communication, Persuasion & Taste](/wiki/communication-persuasion-and-taste). |

## Source quality guide

- `primary`: official documents, standards, datasets, laws, original research, first-party technical docs.
- `credible_secondary`: established institutions, expert reports, high-quality journalism, serious practitioner analysis.
- `useful_secondary`: plausible explainers or case studies that add structure but need corroboration.
- `useful_practitioner_signal`: useful market or workflow signal with claims that should not be repeated unverified.
- `thin_or_unknown`: keep only if it contributes a concrete lead, example, or question.
